# Research: Procedural sprite & tile asset pipeline (issue #7)

## Summary
For a native-only LÖVE 11.5 top-down tile game with a flat-geometric + neon look, the concrete pipeline is: build each sprite as an `ImageData` pixel-by-pixel in code (0..1 float colors, 0-indexed coords) → `love.graphics.newImage(imageData)`; render the static tile grid with one `SpriteBatch` per tile type; compose/glow with a `Canvas` and `love.graphics.setBlendMode("add")`. All generation lives in **`lib/assets.lua`**, built once in `love.load`, per the repo's pinned `.agents/skills/love2d/REFERENCE.md`.

Findings (primary sources: repo REFERENCE.md + love2d.org wiki):
1. **`ImageData:setPixel` → `newImage`** is the whole asset pipeline. `ImageData:setPixel(x,y,r,g,b,a)` is 0-indexed with 0..1 float colors since 11.0; `love.graphics.newImage(imageData)` bridges to GPU and auto-reloads on `setMode`. [ImageData:setPixel](https://love2d.org/wiki/ImageData:setPixel) · [love.graphics.newImage](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newImage)
2. **`SpriteBatch` = many-tiles renderer**: `newSpriteBatch(image, capacity)`, `batch:add(...)`, one `graphics.draw(batch)`; `SpriteBatch:set(id,...)` for per-tile updates. [love.graphics.newSpriteBatch](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newSpriteBatch) · [Tile-based scrolling](https://love2d.org/wiki/Tutorial:Efficient_Tile-based_Scrolling)
3. **`Canvas` = off-screen composition**; default = window pixels, recreate in `love.resize`. [love.graphics.newCanvas](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newCanvas)
4. **Neon glow = `setBlendMode("add")`** + an alpha-falloff halo baked into the ImageData. [BlendMode](https://love2d.org/wiki/BlendMode)
5. **Flat-at-small-size**: 2–3 px opaque core + 2–3 px glow falloff on a dark floor/wall base; `love.math.noise` is fine for ambient floor texture only.

**Proposed primitives (owned by `lib/assets.lua`):** floor, wall tiles; player, enemy_chaser/shooter/tank, projectile sprites; plus tintable `glow` and `particle1` — all 16×16 ImageData with per-artifact `setPixel` loops, neon palette, and a SpriteBatch rendering pattern (full code in the saved note).

# Research: Procedural sprite & tile asset pipeline (issue #7)

## Summary
For a native-only LÖVE 11.5 top-down tile game with a flat-geometric + neon look, the concrete pipeline is: build each sprite as an `ImageData` pixel-by-pixel in code (0..1 float colors, 0-indexed coords) → `love.graphics.newImage(imageData)`; render the static tile grid with one `SpriteBatch` per tile type; compose/glow with a `Canvas` and `love.graphics.setBlendMode("add")`. All generation lives in **`lib/assets.lua`**, built once in `love.load`, per the repo's pinned `.agents/skills/love2d/REFERENCE.md`.

Findings (primary sources: repo REFERENCE.md + love2d.org wiki):
1. **`ImageData:setPixel` → `newImage`** is the whole asset pipeline. `ImageData:setPixel(x,y,r,g,b,a)` is 0-indexed with 0..1 float colors since 11.0; `love.graphics.newImage(imageData)` bridges to GPU and auto-reloads on `setMode`. [ImageData:setPixel](https://love2d.org/wiki/ImageData:setPixel) · [love.graphics.newImage](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newImage)
2. **`SpriteBatch` = many-tiles renderer**: `newSpriteBatch(image, capacity)`, `batch:add(...)`, one `graphics.draw(batch)`; `SpriteBatch:set(id,...)` for per-tile updates. [love.graphics.newSpriteBatch](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newSpriteBatch) · [Tile-based scrolling](https://love2d.org/wiki/Tutorial:Efficient_Tile-based_Scrolling)
3. **`Canvas` = off-screen composition**; default = window pixels, recreate in `love.resize`. [love.graphics.newCanvas](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.newCanvas)
4. **Neon glow = `setBlendMode("add")`** + an alpha-falloff halo baked into the ImageData. [BlendMode](https://love2d.org/wiki/BlendMode)
5. **Flat-at-small-size**: 2–3 px opaque core + 2–3 px glow falloff on a dark floor/wall base; `love.math.noise` is fine for ambient floor texture only.

**Proposed primitives (owned by `lib/assets.lua`):** floor, wall tiles; player, enemy_chaser/shooter/tank, projectile sprites; plus tintable `glow` and `particle1` — all 16×16 ImageData with per-artifact `setPixel` loops, neon palette, and a SpriteBatch rendering pattern (full code in the saved note).
